stem: Why is celecoxib associated with more cardiovascular events than its GI profile would suggest?

distractors.text: TXA2 falls while PGI2 is preserved
distractors.why: Reversed: COX-1 (platelet TXA2) is spared.

distractors.text: It blocks COX-1 more than COX-2
distractors.why: Celecoxib selectively blocks COX-2.

distractors.text: It depletes glutathione in the heart
distractors.why: Glutathione depletion is acetaminophen overdose.

distractors.text: It raises renal blood flow excessively
distractors.why: NSAIDs lower renal blood flow; the kidney is still affected.

why_correct: Celecoxib blocks COX-2, lowering prostacyclin (PGI2) without a matching drop in platelet thromboxane (TXA2, made by spared COX-1) — the balance tips toward clotting.
takeaway: Celecoxib: GI ↓ (COX-1 spared), CV ↑ (PGI2 ↓, TXA2 kept), kidney still affected.
discriminator: Nonselective NSAIDs lower TXA2 too (bleeding risk); celecoxib does not.

stem: Which sequence describes joint destruction in rheumatoid arthritis, as opposed to osteoarthritis?
correct: Synovitis forms a pannus; TNF-α and IL-6 drive erosion

distractors.text: Mechanical wear degrades cartilage; osteophytes form
distractors.why: That is the osteoarthritis sequence.

distractors.text: Uric acid crystals deposit and trigger a flare
distractors.why: Gout is taught in Session 2, not RA.

distractors.text: NAPQI binds proteins in the synovial lining
distractors.why: NAPQI is acetaminophen's toxic metabolite.

distractors.text: Prostaglandin loss thins the gastric mucosa
distractors.why: That describes NSAID GI injury.

why_correct: RA is autoimmune: immune activation causes synovitis with pannus formation that erodes cartilage and bone, with TNF-α and IL-6 driving inflammation and damage — the cytokines biologics target.
takeaway: OA = mechanical wear → cartilage loss → osteophytes. RA = immune synovitis → pannus → TNF-α/IL-6 erosion.
discriminator: The RA cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6) are exactly what TNF inhibitors and tocilizumab block.
